correctness.rationale: Plancherel with the stated pi^(-1) norm gives 2 * integral_0^infinity x^alpha exp(-2xt) dx = Gamma(alpha+1)/[2^alpha t^(alpha+1)], as required by weighted Paley–Wiener. In the Laplace model one step shifts t to t+b with input amplitude exp(-at). Iteration sums t,t+b,...,t+(n-1)b and gives amplitude exp(-ant-abn(n-1)/2). The shifted density contributes (t/(t+nb))^eta to the norm ratio. Its continuous essential supremum is one on either axis; in the open quadrant the log derivative -an+eta*nb/[t(t+nb)] has a unique zero, giving the stated rationalized root. The expansion t_n=eta/(an)+O(n^-3) gives ant_n=eta+O(n^-2) and t_n/(t_n+nb)=eta/(ab n^2)*(1+O(n^-2)), so both the prefactor and relative error follow. For each power, an infinite orthonormal sequence supported on a bounded near-maximizer interval is weakly null; compact operators kill its norm in the limit. This supplies both the finite-rank and essential-norm lower bound for all j and noncompactness. The interior radii vanish by the power norm and the quotient norm bound; the identity and the b=0 multiplier give the first two spectral rows. If a=0<b, the fibers t=r+kb, 0<r<b, carry normalized shifts with weights ((r+kb)/(r+(k+1)b))^eta. For |lambda|<1, their adjoints have eigenvectors lambda^k ((r+kb)/r)^eta times arbitrary L^2 base data on b/2<r<b, uniformly summable there. Infinite-dimensional adjoint kernel gives non-Fredholmness for the conjugate parameter; closure and norm one give both disks. For fixed n and a,b>0, evaluating the ratio at t=sqrt(b/a) lower-bounds it by exp(-abn(n-1)/2-n sqrt(ab))/(1+n sqrt(ab))^eta, confirming convergence to one as ab->0 from the quadrant. The 1158 checks in the frozen audit and inspected CHECK.py are finite corroboration, not a fresh run or proof of the spectrum.
